data.title: Costco Stock (COST) in Focus as Company Limits Motor Oil Purchases
data.description:
Costco Wholesale (COST) has raised prices and begun to limit purchases of motor oil sold at its U.S. stores as lubricant supplies tighten. The warehouse club has raised the price of its Kirkland Signature full-synthetic motor oil and introduced purchase limits. The 10-quart package sold at Costco, which contains two five-quart bottles, now sells for $57.99, nearly double its previous price of $30.

At the same time, customers of Costco are being limited to two packages of the motor oil per week, with some locations setting a limit of one purchase at a time. Costco has also imposed limits on the Mobil 1 full-synthetic six-quart packs of motor oil that it sells in the U.S., with the price for that product now set at $44.

Rising Oil Prices Hit Costco

Other major sellers of motor oil such as Walmart (WMT), Amazon (AMZN), and AutoZone (AZO) do not appear to have followed Costco (COST) yet in significantly hiking motor oil prices or limiting purchases.

data.title: Dow Jones: DJIA Dips on AI Development Warnings as Rate Hike Odds Advance
data.description:
The Dow Jones (DJIA) is down 0.12% on Monday after OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei voiced concerns about the speed of AI advancements. In an X post, Altman cautioned that humanity "could lose control of the future to AI" without proper safeguards. Furthermore, he said a concentration of AI under one person or company could lead to an "extremely dystopian" outcome.

Meanwhile, Amodei warned in a 3,800-word essay that developing AI irresponsibly could cause economic disruption and more cybersecurity attacks. "We must slow the pace at which we improve the capabilities of AI models," he wrote.

President Trump downplayed the concerns of the two leaders, arguing that the only guardrails necessary are a "STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades!" Over the weekend, he cautioned that slowing down the pace of AI could cause China to overtake the U.S. in the industry.

data.title: Boeing Stock (NYSE:BA) Notches Up, SPEEA Contract Deal Looks Close
data.description:
Recently, we heard about aerospace stock Boeing (BA) and its move to restart negotiations again with the Society of Professional Engineering Employees in Aerospace (SPEEA). The first move ended with SPEEA rejecting the contract rather heavily, and so, Boeing made another offer. It was Boeing's final offer, noted a report from Fox 13 in Seattle, and it seems to have done the job. Boeing shares ticked up fractionally in Monday afternoon's trading. Boeing has seen a 2.46% loss in its share price over the past year.

It Just Might Be Over

SPEEA's leadership recommended approval of the deal, which Boeing called its "final contract offer" according to Fox 13. The new contract offer calls for a guaranteed 10% wage hike after the contract is approved, and another 4% increase to kick in starting with March 2027. There were also revisions to some of the language on work-from-home policies, as well as overtime limits for some parts of the union. A set of "wage pools" was also established for the three years following the 2027 raises.

Boeing's vice president and functional chief engineer for Production Engineering, Ben Nimmergut, noted, "Our final contract offer addresses the top priorities identified by our employees and SPEEA's bargaining teams, including an immediate wage increase and larger wage pools with guarantees. We're optimistic this will allow all of us to focus on the important work ahead."

data.title: Google Stock (GOOGL) Pops 3% as Company Plans to Build an AI Data Center in New Mexico
data.description:
The stock of Google's parent company Alphabet (GOOGL) is up 3% on reports that company is planning to build an artificial intelligence (AI) data center in New Mexico. Multiple media reports say that Alphabet is considering building a new large-scale data center in Lea County, New Mexico, and is focused on community outreach as a key part of the project's development.

"Our goal in Lea County is simple: serve as long-term partners who can be counted on to do the right thing in support of the places we call home," said Alphabet said in a blog post about the proposed project. "That includes responsibly managing vital water resources, paying for 100% of the energy we use and infrastructure we need, and showing up as active members of the community."

An AI Slowdown?

News that Alphabet is planning a new data center that will potentially cost billions of dollar to build and operate comes on the day when Wall Street is trying assess whether companies will slow their progress on developing AI technologies. In recent days, Dario Amodei, the CEO of AI startup Anthropic has called for a slowdown in developing the technology, and OpenAI announced that it is canceling its planned initial public offering (IPO) that had been planned for this year.

data.title: ServiceNow Stock Is Surging Today, Is the Stock Still a Buy? Needham Weighs In
data.description:
AI stocks are down, which therefore means software stocks are up. That scenario appears to be playing out again in Monday's trading following calls from AI leaders to slow down the development of AI.

Against this backdrop, ServiceNow (NYSE:NOW) shares, which often seem to move in the opposite direction of AI stalwarts, are up by 8%.

The company has also received a positive assessment from Needham analyst Mike Cikos, who ranks among the top 4% of analysts tracked by TipRanks. Cikos believes investors are becoming more receptive to software stocks as they reassess the importance of established enterprise platforms, the difficulty of displacing leading vendors and the way businesses are making technology purchasing decisions.

After speaking with the company, Cikos came away more positive on its strategy and product roadmap, particularly its opportunity in AI governance. As businesses deploy more AI agents, controlling those systems, monitoring their activity and managing the associated security risks are becoming major challenges. Cikos believes ServiceNow is well placed to address them because of its long-standing role in managing enterprise workflows and IT infrastructure.

One area attracting particular attention is the company's AI Control Tower, which Cikos expects to see sustained adoption as customers look for ways to manage the full lifecycle of AI agents and assess whether their AI investments are delivering meaningful returns.

The 5-star analyst also sees Action Fabric as an important part of ServiceNow's AI strategy. The recent Salesforce-Anthropic Claudeforce initiative highlights a broader change in how enterprises may interact with software, with AI assistants potentially becoming an alternative way to access corporate data and applications. Cikos believes this does not necessarily undermine established software providers. ServiceNow still controls important workflows, data and business processes, while Moveworks remains his "preferred front door" for end users because of its integration with the platform.

More broadly, Cikos sees the rise of AI agents as potentially reinforcing the importance of established enterprise software. Although users might interact with applications through AI rather than traditional interfaces, the underlying data, permissions and workflows still need to sit somewhere. That leaves ServiceNow with an important role in managing those processes as businesses adopt more AI.

Cikos also points to recent customer renewals as another positive signal. ServiceNow's U.S. federal government customers renewed contracts earlier than expected, contributing around 100 basis points to Q2 subscription revenue outperformance. Management said those decisions were not related to pricing changes or new products, which Cikos sees as evidence of underlying customer demand. He believes the renewals also reflect the importance enterprises place on zero-trust security and the potential benefits of ServiceNow's Armis acquisition.

To this end, Cikos rates NOW stock a Buy, while his price target goes from $115 to $155, implying shares will gain 9% over the one-year timeframe. (To watch Cikos' track record, click here)

26 other analysts join Cikos in the bull camp, while 1 Hold and 2 Sells can't detract from a Strong Buy consensus rating. However, the $141.75 average price target suggests the shares are fully valued. (See NOW stock forecast)

data.title: Nvidia Stock (NVDA) Falls Despite a Quantum Computing Update
data.description:
Nvidia (NVDA) stock was down 2.96% on Monday, even after the company announced the expansion of an open-source AI project. The chipmaker is expanding its CUDA-Q open-source platform with CUDA-Q Logical, an orchestration layer built to help researchers develop apps for fault-tolerant quantum computers.

According to Nvidia, the new tool lets teams model and manage parts of a quantum system. It also lets them switch between system options to find setups that work well with logical qubits. Nvidia says this could help cut the time needed to build useful quantum-GPU systems.

The need for this work comes from the limits of physical qubits. Fault-tolerant systems use logical qubits to help deal with errors and run larger tasks. Iceberg Quantum used CUDA-Q Logical to model its fault-tolerant design for Diraq's qubits. The work showed that 1,000 logical qubits could be made with 150,000 physical qubits, about 10 times fewer than prior estimates.

Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory also used the tool to test qubits, run times and error-correction methods across many system designs. The lab cut its work time from about five months to three weeks. On that same note, Sandia National Laboratories is using CUDA-Q as part of QUOPS, a new open benchmark for tracking the gains made by quantum computing systems. Early tests cover QPUs from Alphabet's (GOOGL) Google, IBM (IBM) and Quantinuum (QNT).

"Quantum computing is maturing into an era of logical qubits," said Timothy Costa, vice president and general manager of quantum at Nvidia. He said CUDA-Q Logical gives teams a way to test full systems across qubit types and designs. Nvidia also pointed to wider use of its quantum tools, such as NVQLink, Nvidia Ising and cuQuantum. CUDA-Q Logical is now open on GitHub, while QUOPS also has a public reference build.

Why Was Nvidia Stock Down Today?

Nvidia stock was down despite its quantum computing update today. That's because there are currently heated arguments about AI advancements. Some AI company CEOs are calling for a slowdown in AI development. On the other hand, some company leaders and government officials want AI development to continue at a brisk pace.

Is Nvidia Stock a Buy, Sell, or Hold?

Turning to Wall Street, the analysts' consensus rating for Nvidia is Strong Buy, based on 30 Buy ratings over the past three months. With that comes an average NVDA stock price target of $324.30, representing a potential 52.72% upside for the shares. (See NVDA Stock Forecast)
